A very interesting one I read was Blindness by José Saramago. Where an epidemic of blindness struck the world that spread like a disease.

I was really annoyed by that book. Saramago went for a postmodern thing where he never named the city or the country where the story took place, not even giving it a fictional name. The obvious reason was so the reader could understand the story as happening anywhere in the world, it could happen in any city. But the use of this device was so forced, I felt it weakened the story - these weren't real characters in a real world, they were just paper cutouts who had no real lives, and Saramago had nothing to say about culture in the real world, which is pretty strange because the characters in the story make moral decisions that kind of need a cultural background to make them believable.
